title: Two-Sample Rates for Transporting Treatment Effects to Targets on Unknown Manifolds
gap_reasons: Closest bundle result: Federer 1959, Lemma 5.2, pp. 451-453, hypotheses (1)-(9), parametrizes normals using local frames and gives volume of {x: distance_C(x)<=r, nearest_C(x) in g(Q)} for a bounded Borel base Q. Corollary 5.3, p.454, specializes this to a class-1 submanifold. Neither states the formula for arbitrary Borel H inside the normal disk bundle required by ReachNormalCoordinates and equation (9) of UniformSmallBall.

Residual research obligations remain: normal-bundle manifold/trivializations, identification of Hausdorff measure with base area times Euclidean fiber volume, arbitrary-H localization, Jacobian a^k det(I-aS_u), and extension/null-boundary treatment for a C2 manifold with boundary. These are substantial derivations, not a faithful cited-gate transcription.
proof_attempt_summary: Formalization reached 59 proof iterations before the fixed-profile regularity substrate checkpoint. A four-round study proved and promoted eleven generic calculus modules; bounded research integration then proved the unchanged witness regularity certificate, with no new assumptions or axioms. The remaining normal-bundle area formula cannot be transcribed from the audited primary statements without substantial new geometry, so the supervisor authorized failed banking with nine proof holes and the flagship still depending on sorryAx.
tldr: A randomized source sample identifies a smooth conditional treatment effect, while an independent target sample determines where that effect must be averaged. The target may lie on an unknown compact connected \(C^2\) manifold or in its normal tube, with separate manifold and boundary reach bounds and public volume bounds. A reach-based auxiliary-tube argument supplies public local-mass control without atlas-count or slope restrictions. Under the public feasibility inequality placing the centered flat disk and its full tube inside the covariate cube, the radius-uniform minimax and honest-length frontier is \(\max\{N^{-1/2},\min[n^{-s/(2s+d-m)},(n\rho^{d-m})^{-1/2}],(nN)^{-s/(2s+d)}\}\). A boundary-corrected cross-sample kernel attains it, and a paired-sign fixed-count experiment gives the matching two-sample term. For \(N=n^{\gamma+o(1)}\), the strict interaction window at \(\rho=0\) is nonempty exactly when \(m>2s\), whereas at every fixed \(\rho>0\) it is nonempty exactly when \(d>2s\); shrinking radii interpolate at the elbow \(\rho_n=n^{-1/(2s+d-m)+o(1)}\).
gap: Known-weight submanifold integration omits uncertainty in the target law, while ordinary transported-ATE and dominated moment-shift theory require an ambient likelihood-ratio representation that fails at zero radius. Zhang et al., Theorem 4, gives an unknown-law plug-in truncated upper bound with target Monte Carlo error but no matching unknown-law lower bound. Pathak, Ma, and Wainwright and Kpotufe and Martinet allow singular covariate shift through ball-mass ratios or transfer exponents, but their minimax experiments place labels in the target sample and study regression or classification risk rather than a source-labelled plus target-unlabeled scalar functional and honest interval. Jin and Syrgkanis match the source-response plus target-covariate observation pattern for a scalar linear functional, but their anchored structure-agnostic nuisance-rate theorems are dominated-reference oracle bounds rather than a Hölder singular-tube frontier or honest-length result.
fill: The project gives primitive feasibility inequalities and a concrete legal flat submodel, derives a public small-ball certificate from noncollapsing geometry, constructs one observable cross-sample estimator and finite-sample interval, and proves matching risk and connected-length lower bounds with normalized thin and thick tube alternatives in the exact fixed-count experiment.
